items.note: Quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study of 96 graphic design students in a control group and a GenAI group, with originality and project thinking scored by two external judges on analytic rubrics (abstract in Spanish; non-random group assignment).

Randomised controlled trial with 1190 business undergraduates in Marketing, Management, and Entrepreneurship, ChatGPT versus no ChatGPT, with creativity scored for fluency, originality, and elaboration; effects differ by discipline.

Within-subjects experiment where 36 novice designers made advertisements with and without GenAI, and clients and online volunteers rated the designs for creativity, novelty, usefulness, and appeal; also measures participants' divergent thinking; abstract from Semantic Scholar; order randomization not stated; below 50 participants.

Between-subjects essay-writing study (n = 253) varying the stage of AI support (planning, drafting, revising, presumably against no AI); main outcome is ownership, but essay quality is also scored and rises with AI contributions.

Online experiment in which 276 people refined innovation-challenge ideas alone, with AI-generated text, or with AI-generated images; idea creativity is rated (image support 18 percent less creative than text support) and effort is measured.

Systematic literature review on how generative AI affects the creative thinking of STEAM learners in higher education; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, web search), classified from the title.

Controlled experiment with 40 Chinese GFL undergraduates writing under human-only, human-LLM, or LLM-only conditions, with creativity scored on a Torrance-inspired rubric; below 50 participants and the LLM-only arm is an AI-versus-human comparison.

Observational analysis of 41.3 million natural-science papers that links AI-augmented research to higher individual impact but a 4.63 percent contraction in topics studied and less follow-on engagement; AI tools span distinct eras of AI, not generative AI specifically (abstract from Europe PMC).

Research Policy paper on human-AI complementarities in innovation search; abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect, web search), so the design is unknown and the verdict follows the doubt rule; full text needed to confirm human participants and a generative-AI comparison.

In-person pilot (N = 62) of a two-player Alternate Uses Test comparing a GPT-4 partner with a human partner under matched conditions plus non-interactive baselines, with originality scored; mainly a testbed paper, so the comparison design needs checking in the full text.
